policy: Second intensive review. Classifier scores and pre-existing malicious labels were leads, not behavioral evidence. No external corroboration of these exact specimen convictions was found or assumed.

samples.marker: CI publish bridge: shell poisoning and token relay; fix overclaims
samples.identification: Exported JavaScript CI publish-bridge and credential-handoff functions; no verified package identity
paths: Module evaluation reads NPM_TOKEN or NODE_AUTH_TOKEN and defines functions; it invokes no exported function.
poisonReleaseEnv appends BASH_ENV=<cwd>/.github/scripts/publish-bridge.sh plus a real newline to GITHUB_ENV.
collectStageZero returns false unless the exact package-name and publish-timeout environment gates hold. It launches the bridge with stage0, --config64 and Base64 JSON {"schema":"test.v1"}.

The child receives the captured npm token, an empty BASH_ENV and supplied event text. Streams are ignored; timeout is 15 seconds, followed by SIGTERM. Only successful status zero returns true; other results log an error and return false.
dropBridge conditionally spawns rm -f on the bridge and sets process.exitCode=1. It neither creates the bridge nor writes the unused /tmp marker.
samples.obfuscation: Plain source. Base64 is configuration JSON, not executable payload concealment.
samples.judgement: Malicious intent is supported by the deliberate later-step startup redirection, credential handoff/receipt acknowledgement, suppressed child output and deletion/failure path. The source comments explicitly describe interception and a collector. These facts outweigh the validation-helper label. No invocation, deployed bridge, registry metadata or external attribution is supplied; network exfiltration and successful compromise cannot be established.
samples.coverage: Two former hostile rules only required startup/CI/credential references (plus generic process evidence). Ordinary release automation satisfies them, including the pre-existing bridge.js fixture. They are preserved as accurately named notable co-occurrence traits. New checks establish actual startup-file append, explicit child-token option, rm -f invocation, nonzero exit assignment and staged-config spawnSync; the combined cleanup pattern is suspicious.
samples.hostile_goal_limit: No unambiguous third (or even standalone hostile) result is established by generalizable byte matchers here: BASH_ENV setup, credential forwarding and cleanup also occur in legitimate automation. The new suspicious combination captures their relationship without claiming network theft. Missing bridge code blocks source-to-network, downloaded-payload and downstream-execution detections. Comments inform the analyst verdict but cannot turn ordinary primitives into hostile matchers.

samples.marker: CloudSync VBS: minute persistence and hidden policy-bypass execution
samples.identification: CloudSyncMaintenance VBScript Task Scheduler installer and PowerShell launcher; claimed name/author are not verified product provenance
paths: Expands APPDATA and constructs cloud-sync.vbs and cloud-sync.ps1 paths without creating or copying either file.
Uses Schedule.Service, a new task definition, trigger type 1 (time), executable action type 0, Enabled and StartWhenAvailable, and PT1M repetition.
Registers/updates a task with flags 6 and logon type 3 (interactive token), launching explorer.exe with the quoted VBS loader path. RegistrationInfo.Author="System" does not request SYSTEM execution.
Independently launches powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <AppData stage>, using WScript.Shell.Run with window style 0 and wait=False.
Unpadded date/time construction, absent scripts or host associations can affect runtime success; static code still establishes the intended registration and hidden launch.
samples.obfuscation: No obfuscation or encoded payload. Ordinary environment expansion and string concatenation construct the paths.
samples.judgement: The one-minute Explorer-mediated AppData script activation and immediate hidden policy-bypass PowerShell launch together are likely an implant installer. No legitimate CloudSync distribution, payload scripts, user authorization or deployment record is supplied. Cosmetic author/name fields do not establish privilege escalation or benign provenance.
samples.coverage: Time-triggered persistence moves from login to system scheduled-task persistence. The second hostile finding now requires actual hidden PowerShell -File invocation and is filed under execution/interpreter, rather than claiming nonexistent payload staging or C2. Rapid repetition alone is notable scheduling configuration. Generic quoted Arguments are relocated from shortcut creation to process arguments; the ordinary Explorer-folder task no longer triggers hostile script persistence. WSH Run uses the existing canonical execution matcher; no command-parsing shell is inferred.
samples.hostile_goal_limit: Two distinct hostile results are supported: recurring script activation and immediate hidden PowerShell script execution. The source contains no download, stage-file write, self-copy, credential collection or network operation from which to add further hostile detections. Relevant hidden-launch and policy-override capabilities remain notable.

samples.marker: RouterOS fixture: harness-only exploit demo; retain technique coverage
samples.identification: Explicit synthetic RouterOS SSH PTY policy-injection test fixture
paths: The module defines one function and contains no invocation, imports, socket construction, target address or connection setup. Its docstring explicitly says the transport/channel come from a test harness.
When invoked, authenticates on the supplied transport using username -7 and the caller password, opens a session, requests a VT100 PTY and invokes the shell.
Builds effective_name.encode()+NUL+decimal policy_mask.encode()+NUL+EOT+EOT, then sends that actual record.
Sends a RouterOS /user add command with a fixed lab-labelled password and group=full. The effective user and mask are caller-selected, and neither exploit success nor a live device is demonstrated.
samples.obfuscation: No obfuscation. NUL/EOT bytes form the exploit protocol record and terminal delimiters.
samples.judgement: BENIGN as an explicitly labelled harness fixture: import is inert, all transport is caller-supplied, the credential is labelled lab-only, and no targeting/deployment behavior is included. The function nevertheless implements attack-relevant behavior. A substituted real transport would make it dangerous; the benign verdict therefore retains accurate hostile technique findings. No external source corroborates malicious deployment of this exact specimen.
samples.coverage: The actual authority manipulation moves to privilege-escalation/exploit/login; account creation alongside exploitation remains persistence. Generic NUL construction, punctuation-user/auth co-occurrence and RouterOS full-account management move to neutral capability homes. New flow checks bind the negative numeric username to auth_password and NUL/EOT literals to send calls. Ordinary punctuation usernames, unsent records and normal-username binary terminal sends do not satisfy the hostile rule.
samples.hostile_goal_limit: Not applicable to the BENIGN judgement; two accurate hostile technique findings and one suspicious crafted-username finding are intentionally retained.

weakening_and_removal_audit.claim: Startup/CI/secret references prove shell hijacking; adding generic process references proves secret relay.
weakening_and_removal_audit.counterevidence: Existing testdata/bash-env-ci/bridge.js and the ordinary npm publish control satisfy these matchers without establishing attacker code, interception or exfiltration.
weakening_and_removal_audit.correction: Move the observations to notable os/env/cicd co-occurrence rules; add precise suspicious startup/token/cleanup coverage instead of preserving unsupported hostile weights.

weakening_and_removal_audit.claim: Short repetition is suspicious login persistence.
weakening_and_removal_audit.counterevidence: A time trigger is not a login trigger; ordinary task repetition, including the Explorer-folder control, can run every minute.
weakening_and_removal_audit.correction: Retain the interval as notable OS scheduling configuration and move the admitted script persistence to system/scheduled-task.

weakening_and_removal_audit.claim: Any quoted Arguments assignment creates a shortcut.
weakening_and_removal_audit.counterevidence: This specimen assigns IExecAction.Arguments; no CreateShortcut call exists.
weakening_and_removal_audit.correction: Preserve the exact matcher under process/argument/positional and update shortcut consumers.

weakening_and_removal_audit.claim: A PowerShell policy-override string and zero-style Run near a task prove an AppData staged payload loader.
weakening_and_removal_audit.counterevidence: No file write or staging exists and the former matcher did not require a PowerShell file launch.
weakening_and_removal_audit.correction: Require WSH hidden Run plus PowerShell -File text, and relocate to execution/interpreter.

weakening_and_removal_audit.claim: NUL record construction, generic punctuation usernames near auth, or full-account management independently prove exploitation or unwanted persistence.
weakening_and_removal_audit.counterevidence: Unsent-record, ordinary-auth and ordinary-NUL-terminal controls; benign appliance provisioning can add full accounts.
weakening_and_removal_audit.correction: Retain capabilities in neutral homes; require a sent NUL/EOT record and a negative numeric username actually supplied to auth for the exploit result.

weakening_and_removal_audit.claim: The legacy WScript.Shell .Run token rule is an independent shell launch mechanism.
weakening_and_removal_audit.counterevidence: WshShell.Run starts an image; it need not invoke a shell, and the old token could match a member mention without invocation. Actual calls in this sample and the retained fixtures are already covered by wsh-progid-near-run.
weakening_and_removal_audit.correction: Consolidate consumers onto that canonical exec matcher rather than add a duplicate at a new path.

additional_placement_audit: The capped exec leaf was reviewed. HTML Help Item1 numeric entities prove an encoding property, not program execution; move this existing matcher unchanged to metadata/lang/encoding and update its CHM consumer.

The capped scheduled-task leaf was reviewed. A system-like /tn argument is an argument property, not task registration; move unchanged to process/argument/positional and preserve the masquerade consumers. No limits were raised and no arbitrary taxonomy split was introduced.
Node exit-status and NUL-record construction checks use parsed assignments/operators to avoid treating comment mentions as executed operations.

outside_batch_checks.known_fixture: Existing GitHub shell-payload staging fixture retains its suspicious attack finding. The simplistic prior bridge.js retains all supported capabilities but loses its two unsupported hostile claims.
outside_batch_checks.comparison: Against a HEAD snapshot of the old traits, this upstream exploit had zero hostile findings and two suspicious findings. The corrected rules produce two hostile and two suspicious findings, recognizing separately assembled record bytes. The SSH/PTY span was expanded from 32 to 64 lines because authentication and the transmitted policy frame are 45 lines apart in the upstream function. This adds real attack coverage while the normal-username and unsent controls stay negative.
outside_batch_checks.interpretation: These sources confirm the technique, not malicious deployment or registry provenance of the supplied fixture.

validation.focused_suite: 11 cases passed in verify.py, including renamed and quoted-key variants and benign boundary controls.
validation.execution_traces: QuickJS 1.19.4 with inert filesystem/process stubs and Python recording transport/channel objects; all assertions passed. No sample command, real SSH session or payload was executed.
validation.classifier_disagreements: JS and VBS remain below the classifier malicious threshold despite the analyst MALICIOUS judgements. The Python harness remains classifier-positive despite its BENIGN context. JS and Python report incomplete flow queries; they are not clean scans. No inaccurate trait was restored to manipulate a score.
validation.final_check: make validate is the final action; its actual result is recorded in the final response.
validation.model_version_limit: Atomscan warns that the installed feature specification is v18 while the current analyzer expects v21; newer features are absent from this model. This is a classifier limitation, separate from YAML correctness.
